scope: Source audit complete for the named 37-file set. Local UI implementation is underway. This audit makes no publication claim and does not represent every source phrase as a completed drill.
method: Opened all36 files in the provided local source folder plus the separately resolved one-page Library recap of printed textbook p224. Read native PDF text by page and PPTX/DOCX XML by slide/body block, including tables.
Inspected all substantive embedded teaching images plus scanned pages/JPEG handouts. Decorative destination photos are outside teaching-text transcription.

Compared original native text to old extracts. Run-split whitespace was ignored for PPTX/DOCX fidelity checks; native text matches for five available slide extracts and Lesson2 DOCX. Lesson5 slide extract was missing.
Source locators are 1-based. A textbook page number is distinguished from the physical PDF page and from DOCX body-block numbering.

Original wording is preserved in raw extraction files. Inventory wording folds line wrapping and occasionally standardises apostrophe style; such variants are called out. Source grammar claims are not automatically endorsed.
This ledger inventories source content. It does not claim that source phrases are missing from existing site teaching text; current implementation coverage is a separate comparison.

future_ingestion_rules.rule: Assign an immutable source ID to the original file. Retain original filename, extension, byte count, SHA-256 and provider identity where available. Never use a filename stem alone as identity.

Compare original hashes before merging duplicate uploads. Keep duplicate provenance when filenames or providers differ. Append new source IDs; never renumber existing src-, phrase-, use- or homework IDs.
Keep PDF, PPTX and DOCX extracts separate even when filename stems match. Read PPTX slides in numeric slide order and concatenate text runs inside their original paragraphs and table cells.
Store 1-based PDF page or PPTX slide and distinguish physical file page from printed textbook page. For unrendered DOCX use body-block locators and do not claim verified pagination.

Visually inspect embedded teaching images, scanned tables and image-only pages. Retain exact image text, visible source credit and uncertainty. Native text extraction alone does not establish completeness.
Inspect original speaker-note XML or the native presentation notes, including notes linked to image-only slides. Record whether notes add teaching content or contain only placeholders.
Preserve source wording, variants and typos in the audit. Record a separate correction or adaptation for teaching content, with its rationale. Do not silently combine contradictory examples.

Separate assigned homework, classwork and optional reference revision. Retain exact book page/exercise references. If the original task page or audio is missing, record the assignment without inventing its questions or answers.

A phrase labelled verbatim must match the cited original. Conjugation changes, simplified English, new subjects and other adaptations must be labelled adapted or supplementary. Keep existing stable phrase IDs when wording remains the same.
Treat user-reported material as unverified until an original source is examined. Do not silently replace pendere with prendere or invent Laura’s examples.

Keep source-inventory counts separate from implemented, tested and published exercise counts. Presence in this ledger does not mean a phrase is missing from existing teaching text or already has a drill.
